title: Container Apps Revisions and Ingress
description: Use revisions for safe deployments and configure ingress rules to expose your Container Apps.

data.text: A revision is an immutable snapshot of your Container App's configuration. When you update your app, Container Apps creates a new revision instead of modifying the existing one. This enables zero-downtime deployments and instant rollbacks.

items: Revisions are immutable snapshots of app configuration
Updating any setting creates a new revision
Traffic can be split between revisions for canary deployments
Rollback is instant - just route traffic back to the previous revision

data.text: Ingress controls how your Container App is exposed. You can choose external ingress (accessible from the internet) or internal ingress (only accessible within the VNet).

data.title: Azure CLI - Deploy with Ingress and Traffic Split
data.content:
# Deploy a new revision with 10% traffic
az containerapp update \
  --name myapp \
  --resource-group myRG \
  --image myregistry.azurecr.io/myapp:2.0 \
  --ingress external \
  --target-port 8080 \
  --revision-suffix v2 \
  --set-env-vars DEPLOYMENT=v2

# Split traffic: 90% to v1, 10% to v2
az containerapp ingress traffic set \
  --name myapp \
  --resource-group myRG \
  --revision-weight v1=90 v2=10

data.title: Canary Deployments
data.text: Use revision-based traffic splitting to roll out new versions gradually. Send 5% of traffic to the new revision first, monitor for issues, then gradually increase to 100%.

data.title: Deploy with Revisions
data.description: Deploy a Container App, update it to create a second revision, and split traffic between them.
steps: Deploy a container app with an initial image
Update the app with a different image to create a new revision
Use `az containerapp revision list` to see both revisions
data.expectedOutcome: You can see both revisions active and traffic is split between them.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Revisions are immutable snapshots enabling safe deployments
Ingress controls how apps are exposed (external, internal, none)
Rolling back is as simple as changing traffic weights
data.takeaway: Revisions make deployments safe and reversible in Container Apps.
